Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask and the requirements doc (helpful). High level answers and what I attached: a simple pricing matrix (redwood_vpc_pricing_matrix.xlsx) showing three illustrative scenarios: pilot (12k tokens/day), production-light (2M tokens/day), and production-heavy (10M tokens/day). Key takeaways:

- Operator license model: predictable fixed monthly cost based on "operator seats" (recommended if you need predictable throughput and want to avoid token-variance billing). Good for heavy, steady workloads (your nightly batch).

- Usage-led + platform fee: lower upfront but token costs add up under heavy usage. Platform fee covers control plane, telemetry, and private deployment orchestration; we offer amortization on platform fee with multi-year commits.

- Hybrid recommendation for HelixCare: operator licenses for batch GPU nodes + usage for spiky API traffic. The attached matrix includes a straight-line 36-month amortization vs up-front platform fee and shows net present cost over 3 years (assumes a conservative 5% discount rate).

Support tiers: short bullets in the sheet; Marissa (cc'd) will follow up with a clearer SRE/oncall breakdown and escalation windows.

If you’re open, let’s schedule a 30–40 minute call Friday to walk the numbers live (I can bring Rishi for the discount waterfall discussion).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Deals — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_vpc_pricing_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 4 tabs)
